query: Which principled stopping rule should govern CT-anchor acquisition (mathematical threshold on expected utility, marginal gain, or calibration target), and how to simulate its operating characteristics?

response.query: Which principled stopping rule should govern CT-anchor acquisition (mathematical threshold on expected utility, marginal gain, or calibration target), and how to simulate its operating characteristics?
response.answer: The principled stopping rule for CT-anchor acquisition is typically the calibration target, which ensures the expected utility threshold is met. Simulation of its operating characteristics involves assessing the accuracy of predictions against actual outcomes.

results.title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; CY 2026 Payment ...
results.content: See *Data.CMS.gov,* Medicare Shared Savings Program, Accountable Care Organizations, Public Use File (by performance year, for PY 2025), available at *https://data.cms.gov/​medicare-shared-savings-program/​accountable-care-organizations.*. Message to the Quality Payment Program listserv on January 4, 2025, entitled “The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is Soliciting Stakeholder Recommendations for Potential Consideration of New Specialty Measure Sets and/or Revisions to the Existing Specialty Measure Sets for the 2026 Performance Year of the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS).”. Section 101(b) of the Medicare Access and CHIP Reauthorization Act of 2015 (MACRA) sunset the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals, set forth at section 1848(o) of the Act. As discussed previously, section 1848(o)(2) of the Act has been incorporated into the MIPS Promoting Interoperability performance category's requirements via section 1848(q)(2)(B)(iv) of the Act. See CY 2017 Quality Payment Program final rule (81 FR 77018 and 77019) for more information regarding the sunsetting of the Medicare EHR Incentive Program for Eligible Professionals.

results.title: Southern Sun | News
results.content: The agreement positions Southern Sun as the official hotel partner of SAFA, providing world-class hospitality services for South Africa’s men’s and women’s national football teams, as well as SAFA’s staff and guests during key tournaments and events. We already operate three full service hotels – The Cullinan, Southern Sun Waterfront and Southern Sun Cape Sun – as well as the recently refurbished SunSquare Cape Town in Gardens and believe the addition of an exciting new product aimed at the limited service market will allow us to provide the full spectrum of products to suit all budgets for both business and leisure travellers.”. With the latest rating representing the first time that we have been audited against the Tourism Scorecard (gazetted in May 2009), our consistently good result, and now receiving this award,  is testament to our commitment and dedication to empowerment in South Africa “, says Graham Wood, Managing Director Southern Sun Hotels.
